'''Sonia Guimarães''' (born 20 June 1956) is a Brazilian physicist. She is a Professor of Physics at the [[Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica]]. She was the first black Brazilian woman to earn a doctorate in physics and has dedicated her career to improving the representation of black Brazilians in academia.

== Early life and education ==
Guimarães was born in [[São Paulo]]. Her father worked on tapestries and her mother was a merchant. At primary school and secondary school Guimarães was always the top of the class, but she experienced racism as a child. She worked part-time during school and used the money that she earned to pay for college.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blackwomenofbrazil.co/sonia-guimaraes-first-black-brazilian-woman/|title=Sonia Guimarães: first black Brazilian woman|last=Travae|first=Marques|date=2012-01-30|website=Black Women Of Brazil|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> Whilst at high school Guimarães wanted to become an engineer, and sat the Mapofei entrance exam that was a requirement for entry to the [[University of São Paulo]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2017/07/25/8-mulheres-negras-cientistas-brasileiras-que-voce-precisa-conhecer/index.html|title=8 mulheres negras cientistas brasileiras que você precisa conhecer|date=2017-07-25|website=Brasil de Fato|language=pt-BR|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> In 1976 she became the first member of her family to attend university when she joined the [[Federal University of São Carlos]]. During her first year she encountered physics for the first time; and during her course on solid state physics decided that she loved the subject.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://brasil.elpais.com/brasil/2017/02/24/ciencia/1487948035_323512.html|title=Quem são as cientistas negras brasileiras?|last=Sanz|first=Beatriz|date=2017-02-28|website=EL PAÍS|language=pt-br|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> She remained there for her master's degree, where she worked on [[ellipsometry]]. After completing her undergraduate degree Guimarães moved to Italy where she joined the [[University of Bologna]] and worked on microelectronics.<ref>{{Cite == Research and career ==
[[File:Prof Sonia Guimarães at left, Silvana Bahia, Jurema Werneck at right.jpg|thumb|Guimarães advocating for black women in 2018 with [[Silvana Bahia]] and [[Jurema Werneck]] of Amnesty International. ]]
Guimarães joined the [[Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica]] in [[São José dos Campos]] in 1993. She was the first black woman to do so, and joined at a time that women were not allowed to enter the ITA. Whilst women were allowed to enter the university toward the end of 1995, they are still underrepresented to this day – from 2013 to 2018 less than 10% of the students who entered the [[Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica]] were women.<ref name=":3" /> Her research considers electron transport in epitaxially grown semiconductor alloys<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" /> and the development of novel materials for sensing applications.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://5wcorreei.com/speaker/sonia-guimaraes/|title=Sônia Guimarães|website=5ª WCORREEI|language=pt-BR|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Guimarães|first1=Sonia|last2=de Lima|first2=Joaquim Tavares|last3=Petoilho|first3=José Carlos|last4=de Lucena|first4=Emerson Ferreira|last5=Hwang|first5=Míriam Kasumi|last6=Campos|first6=Élson|date=2008-04-01|title=Modified LPE system used to diffuse Cd to obtain InSb infrared detectors|url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022024807011657|journal=Journal of Crystal Growth|series=the Proceedings of the 15th International Conference on Crystal Growth (ICCG-15) in conjunction with the International Conference on Vapor Growth and Epitaxy and the US Biennial Workshop on Organometallic Vapor Phase Epitaxy|language=en|volume=310|issue=7|pages=1657–1663|doi=10.1016/j.jcrysgro.2007.11.176|issn=0022-0248|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 2014 Guimarães delivered a [[TED (conference)|TED]] talk "Educação é a única solução" (Education is the only solution).<ref>{{Citation|title=Educação é a única solução {{!}} Sonia Guimarães {{!}} TEDxJardinsWomen|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9XQcFaWb6r4|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

Alongside her academic research Guimarães has worked to improve diversity in Brazilian research.<ref name=":3" /> In particular, she has looked to support women and black people, who make up over half of the Brazilian population but are severely underrepresented in universities. She has given a series of academic lectures about her experiences of racism in academia and the impact of affirmative action programmes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www3.unicentro.br/petfisica/2019/05/23/sonia-guimaraes/|title=Sônia Guimarães|website=GPET Física|language=pt-BR|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://feiradoconhecimento.com.br/fdc-sonia-guimaraes-aponta-caminhos-para-combater-desigualdades-com-ciencia-e-tecnologia/|title=FdC: Sônia Guimarães aponta caminhos para combater desigualdades com Ciência e Tecnologia – Feira do Conhecimento|language=pt-BR|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Trófeu Raça Negra|Black Race Trophy]] in recognition of her advocacy work. In 2019 the [[Instituto Tecnológico de Aeronáutica]] announced that it would join the quota system for black students.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ufca.edu.br/noticias/sonia-guimaraes-abre-ix-artefatos-da-cultura-negra-com-palestra/|title=Sônia Guimarães abre IX Artefatos da Cultura Negra com palestra – Universidade Federal do Cariri|language=pt-BR|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> Whilst Guimarães had considered retiring, she wants to stay there for the first year of quota students.<ref name=":4" />
